PSI is an internal composite of seven personal and knowledge-work evaluations: Agents’ Last Exam, AutomationBench-AA, FocusBench, JobBench, GDP.pdf, VBT, and DRACO.
We use the 105-task Linux set.
Each task is graded by its native evaluation script, which awards partial credit between 0 and 1 without an LLM judge.
AutomationBench-AA evaluates realistic business workflows in a simulated application environment.
the primary metric is its strict pass@1: the share of workflows that pass every end-state assertion
FocusBench is an internal evaluation of personal agentic tasks across a variety of domains like housing, travel, IT, and finance.
It evaluates how well agents can persistently work through real-world blockers across multiple interactions and adapt to dynamically changing environments.
JobBench contains 65 professional tasks across 35 white-collar occupations.
Each task asks the agent to produce a practical work product and is scored against task-specific rubrics.
GDP.pdf evaluates professional work grounded in supplied PDF source material.
The result source is Surge, and the primary metric is Surge’s reported score.
VBT is an internal agentic web-browsing evaluation in which models answer list-style information-seeking questions
DRACO, from Perplexity, is a deep-research benchmark of 100 complex, multi-domain questions.
We run it in a common internal framework, where models answer using browser search, open, and find tools plus code execution in a sandbox.
Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full results are generated with max reasoning effort.
Where a comparable third-party or provider-reported result exists, we use it; otherwise we use the highest of our internally validated run, self-reported score, or official leaderboard score.
Model refusals receive zero credit and remain in the denominator rather than being dropped.
Internally generated competitor runs use common settings where practical but remain best-effort
The model has not been evaluated on all languages contained in the pre-training data.
Performance can vary with quantization, serving configuration, prompts, tools, and the agent harness.

Today, we’re introducing specialized versions of our existing models, trained using Muse Wonder, and rolling them out to people who use Muse and Meta AI.
November 6, 2026 · 2 minute read

Today, we’re excited to introduce the Muse Wonder series with Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, our most capable models that deliver state-of-the-art performance on personal and professional agentic tasks.
And in the future, we’ll be using Muse Wonder to develop specialized models that we can bring to everyone using Muse.
We evaluate focus through FocusBench and sustained execution through SWE-Marathon, which tests work on long-running software projects.
A full report with additional safety evaluations will be available soon.
